question.text: Per Section 3.3.2 of Chapter 3 (Benefits of Registration and Listing on SSE as elucidated by NSE SSE), which of the following is NOT listed as an explicit benefit?

answer.text: Improved market access via a common, structured meeting ground between SEs and investors/donors
Performance-based philanthropy — SSE instils a culture of performance (Social return) driven philanthropy
Minimal registration cost — saves cost for both issuer and investor/donor via minimal fees
Guaranteed tax-free status for all ZCZP subscriptions under Section 10(23C)

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.3.2 lists five NSE SSE benefits: (i) Improved market access, (ii) Synergy between investors and investee, (iii) Performance-based philanthropy, (iv) Minimal registration cost, (v) Additional avenue for Social Enterprises. It does NOT promise a tax-free status for ZCZP subscriptions — tax treatment depends on Section 80G of the donor and independent of SSE listing status. The Trap: Option D mis-states tax law. Section 10(23C) applies to specific trust income, not to donor-side ZCZP subscription treatment. The SIA must not amplify tax claims that aren't in the framework. Cross-Exam Context: V-A / X-A touch 80G and 10(23C) from donor-advisory lens. XXIII tests the FRAMEWORK-level benefits, not donor tax specifics (those are Topic 5 territory). Assessor's Pro-Tip: During investor/donor-facing materials review, strip out any language suggesting SSE listing confers additional tax benefit. If the SE wants to highlight donor tax benefit, it must root that in the specific 12AB + 80G certificates (each donation-level) — never in the SSE registration per se.
